harvest:const.notes:
I wrote truth/entries/const.toml with 30 constant entries and 3 notation entries, all status = "proposed" and ocr = "good". Every value is SI as printed, from Table XXXI (25 entries) or Table XXXIV (eV and u). Locators carry the Rev. Mod. Phys. page, 025010-45 to 025010-51. I generated the file with a script in the scratchpad (gen_const.py). It checked each value, uncertainty and exponent against the printed row, and the anchors were verified by check.py.

Value format: value and uncertainty are strings. For example G is value "6.674 30 × 10^-11" with uncertainty "(15)", which means the standard uncertainty in the last two digits. Exact quantities have uncertainty "exact". Exact quantities printed with an ellipsis, such as hbar, sigma, c1 and c2, keep the "…" in value. The printed relative uncertainty u_r is in each entry's notes.

Constants covered: c, G, h, hbar, e, k_B, N_A, m_e, the electron mass energy equivalent in MeV, m_p, m_n, m_p/m_e, m_u, the unified atomic mass unit u, eV in J, sigma_SB, c1, c2, mu_0, eps_0, alpha, r_e, sigma_e, a_0, R_inf, c R_inf, Rydberg energy in J and in eV, Hartree energy and mu_B.

check.py: `python3 -I truth/check.py` reports no error mentioning const.toml. Its last run still exits non-zero (161 entries, 6 errors) because of duplicate ids in the colour domain (colour.srgb-*, colour.notation-cie-xyz). colour.toml and the new colour_srgb.toml both define them. That is another harvester's file, so I left it alone.

Problems to know about:
- **Symbol conflicts:** eos.toml already uses the symbols c, G, h and m_u with other meanings, and I cannot add conflicts_with there. My notation entries therefore omit c and G (the CGS definitions live in eos.notation-structure) and use "h_P" for the Planck constant. m_u is covered through the "u" symbol. A later pass could add conflicts_with and an adopted flag so the source's own symbols can be used.
- **c1 units:** the unit cell in the text layer is garbled ("½W m2 h"), so units "W m^2" is my reading from the definition 2 pi h c^2. The notes ask for a page-image check.
- **Anchors:** the c1 and R_inf anchors stop before the garbled unit cell (they contain control characters), so they end at "½W m2" and "½m−1".

harvest:condensed.notes:
Wrote 39 entries (36 content, 3 notation), status proposed, domain rt, ids rt.cond-*, and python3 -I truth/check.py reports 0 errors. Every anchor is an exact single-line substring of the .txt, built programmatically. The equations are heavily garbled in the layout text, so most latex was read from page images; those entries are ocr = poor and need a reviewer to confirm against the page images before blessing. Each non-notation entry has a provenance class, since the SCHEMA and check.py now require one (fit entries carry a reimplement route). Coverage:
- Scales: E_ce, E_ci, E_pe, E_C.
- Condensation: the rho_s scaling (with the eta fits in its notes), the Medin and Lai T_crit fit as cited in Potekhin 2012, and the condensation-condition approximation.
- Emissivity: emissivity, Kirchhoff, R_j from amplitudes, and P_lin.
- Dielectric and ions: the dielectric tensor, damping rates, free-ion and fixed-ion approximations, planar patch, and no vacuum polarisation.
- Fits: the full J fit (structure, J_A, J_B, J_C, line L, fixed-ion variant, validity), the mode-1 fit, and one datum entry listing every numeric fit coefficient.
- Thin-atmosphere boundary: inner boundary condition (eqs. 29-30), mode-reflection construction, |r_mj|^2 and phase approximations, truncation, and vacuum-interface approximation.
Two items to watch. First, the index order of r_mj is reversed between Potekhin 2012 (footnote 1) and van Adelsberg 2005 (eq. 6); this is flagged in rt.cond-reflectivity-from-amplitudes. Second, symbols were renamed to avoid conflicts with the eos, gr and colour files (for example R to R_mean, L to L_line, Z to Z_nuc, theta_B to theta_B^(n)). Another harvester adding generic symbols later could still collide. One caveat on completeness: the Medin and Lai T_crit fit is only as cited in Potekhin 2012, because their paper is not in refs/.
